chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no khums in young camels, cattle, and sheep, except what has completed a year in the possession of the man, and there is no khums in their offspring until a year has passed over them."

key_terms.عِنْدَ الرَّجُلِ: in the possession of the man

ai.seo_question: When does khums become due on young livestock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the timing of zakat liability on livestock, specifying that neither young animals nor their offspring incur the tax until a full lunar year (hawl) has passed in the owner's possession. While the current summary mentions khums, this ruling is primarily associated with zakat al-ansab (livestock tax) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the one-fifth share of war booty or surplus wealth. The narration underscores the principle that ownership must be stable and complete for a full cycle before the obligation is triggered, a key criterion in Usul al-Fiqh.
